name: Citigroup

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Global bank holding company: $1.5T deposits, $820B loans, $2.9T assets; five businesses (Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth, US Personal Banking) plus a shrinking All Other. Takes deposits, moves money across borders, trades, lends, advises.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: 3Q26 revenue $23.8B: Services $6.6B (28%), Markets $6.1B (26%), US Consumer Cards $4.7B (20%), Wealth $3.3B (14%), Banking $1.7B (7%), All Other $1.4B (6%). NII $17.0B, 71% of revenue.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Multinationals, banks and governments (Services, Markets, Banking) plus US card holders and affluent households. No single-customer concentration disclosed; nothing found on a top-customer figure. American Airlines co-brand card added in Q2 2026 (partner concentration in cards; partner payments raise costs).

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: Most international US bank: only 31% of 226,000 staff are in the US; 70% of 2025 Services revenue is outside North America ($14.8B of $21.3B). Mexico exposure $80.8B (4.4% of Citi). Banamex 51% owned; Russia exited Jan 2026. Dollar +4.8% in 3m is a translation/earnings headwind and a stress factor for EM clients.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Spread plus fees plus trading. Services is a deposit-and-fee toll road: $1.04T average deposits, TTS $4.9B revenue (+16%), cross-border value $116B (+10%), AUC/A $35T. Markets and Banking are transaction-driven. Cards are spread plus interchange. 3Q26 NIM 2.43% (3Q25 2.40%).

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Efficiency ratio 58.5% (64.7% a year ago incl. Banamex charge); expenses -2% reported, +3% ex-notable; revenue +8% so operating leverage positive. Direct staff 217k vs 227k a year ago (-4%). Transformation spend about $3.3B in 2025, expected to decline over time. Provision $2.6B: net credit losses $2.2B flat, reserve build $369M (+$333M ACL). No guidance hit-rate series found in the filings read.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Inputs: deposits ($1.5T, +9% yoy, driven by Services corporate operating cash, sticky but rate-sensitive), wholesale funding and market access (signal tags: hy_spreads, fed_funds), regulatory capital (CET1 12.8%, about 120bp above requirement), technology/data (transformation, 548 applications retired in 2025). Chokepoints: US-dollar clearing (47M instructions in 3Q) and global custody depend on Citi's own systems; the consent orders are a self-inflicted single point of failure. Pass-through: deposit spreads widened (Services NII +17%, Wealth NII +20%), but cost of interest expense avg 3.77% vs asset yield 5.54% and Fed hike would lift both; card partner payments and rewards rose (USCC non-interest revenue -$758M).

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Services is #1 globally by the company's own account: proprietary Worldlink/cross-border platforms, 90+ country presence and custody scale; RoTCE 31.2% on $34B of tangible equity (+620bp yoy). Differently now: simplification into five businesses, exits (Russia, Poland, Banamex stake sales), AI/tech investment pulled forward.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Citi card and Citigold are household names; 3Q26 US card spend $175B (+11%), co-brand deals with American Airlines and Costco. Consumer brand is mid-tier vs JPM/BAC; Citi is far more visible to corporates than to households. Marketing spend ratio not isolated in what was read.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Rivals: JPM, BAC, HSBC, Standard Chartered, State Street/BNY (custody). Share gains evidenced in Banking ECM (revenue +77%, in the six largest deals) and Services AUC/A +16%; USCC new accounts -4%; Banking lending revenue -16%. Share data vs rivals not published in the sources read.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Services revenue +15% with every driver up (cross-border +10%, commercial card spend +10%, AUC/A +16%); Wealth client investment assets $759B (+15%), net new investment assets $38B in 3Q (vs $19B); prime balances +40%. Market has the stock near 1.1x TBV versus these growth rates.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: 3Q26 RoTCE 11.5% (Q2 13.0%, 3Q25 8.0%); FY2025 8.8%; YTD 2026 EPS $9.07 (+47% ex-notable). Returned $4.1B in 3Q ($3.0B buybacks, $1.1B dividends), 85% payout, CET1 12.8% vs 13.3% a year ago. FCF is not meaningful for a bank. Pay: PSU awards use RoTCE and TBVPS (DEF 14A). Insider ownership figure not extracted from the proxy; nothing found in the lines read. Buybacks at about 1.1x TBV are accretive only if RoTCE stays above about 11%.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Not losing relevance: Services and cards are growing and the strategy is simplification. Risks: consent orders from 2020 still in force (OCC amendment terminated 2025-12-18; 2024 penalties $61M FRB and $75M OCC), OCC order bars significant acquisitions without approval; execution risk in a multiyear transformation 'not linear' by Citi's own words; key-person risk in CEO Fraser; ~$9B Banamex CTA loss to be booked in earnings at deconsolidation (early 2027).

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: No 8-K Item 4.01 or 4.02, no NT 10-K/10-Q, no material weakness in the auditor report (it lists critical audit matters on Level 3 fair values only). 2.06 impairment 8-K 2025-09-24 (Banamex goodwill $726M). SEC comment letters on 2023 10-K (June/July 2024) asked for clearer consent-order disclosure; none newer found. Regulatory penalties 2024 above. Scan covered 2023-11 to 2026-11 via EDGAR submissions index.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat: positive (NII, trading, capital markets; rising card losses a watch). Slowdown: card and EM credit exposure plus a reserve build already under way ($369M); Services deposits stay but spreads fall if rates drop. Stagflation: mixed. Dollar +4.8%: headwind to EM revenue and Banamex CTA, tailwind to cross-border volumes. Hike risk: unrealized AFS losses cited in CET1 (flat QoQ).

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Consent orders (FRB and OCC, Oct 2020) still require quarterly progress reports; OCC can block significant acquisitions. Capital relief: eSLR cut early-adopted 1 Jan 2026 (SLR minimum 4.0% vs 5.0%); FRB final rules 2026-09-30 to reduce SCB volatility. CET1 requirement about 11.6%. Tariff/EM exposure through client flows. No pending antitrust deal docket found.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: $113.33 vs TBVPS $101.59 = 1.12x. At 10% cost of equity and 3% growth that price implies sustainable RoTCE of about 10.8% (11.2% at 0% growth). Actual: 3Q26 11.5%, 2026 YTD about 12.5% (my estimate from reported income to common), FY2025 8.8%, target 11-13% near-term then 14-15%. Fair P/TBV at 11.5% = 1.21x ($123, +9%); at 12.5% = 1.36x ($138, +22%); at FY25 8.8% = 0.83x ($84, -26%). P/E about 11x trailing reported EPS ($10.25) and about 9.4x annualised 2026 YTD EPS. Peers P/TBV: BAC 1.67x, WFC 1.82x, GS 2.35x, MS 3.10x. Citi's own 5-year P/TBV range: not computed (nothing sourced); proxy says stock only recently crossed above tangible book.

status_reason: Price asks only ~10.8% RoTCE vs 11.5% now, but quality is C until returns beat the 10% cost of equity for several quarters and the 2020 consent orders end; no kill-switch rule holds.
the_mistake: The market prices Citi as one ~11%-return bank at 1.1x tangible book, while Services alone earns 31% on $34B of tangible equity and Banking, Cards and Wealth earn 14-22%. The drag is Markets (12.3%) and All Other (-$955M a quarter, mostly Banamex and legacy exits) that fall away as Banamex deconsolidates in early 2027.
what_makes_market_notice: Banamex deconsolidation (expected early 2027, timing subject to change); Q4 results mid-January 2027 showing RoTCE at or above the 11-13% goal; any lifting of the 2020 FRB/OCC consent orders; 2027 stress-test SCB (FRB models finalized 2026-09-30).

feedback.fact: Services deposits $1.04T average (+16% yoy) and cross-border value +10%, USD clearing +5%: corporate cash flows still growing in 3Q26, consistent with overheat hard data.
Reserve build of $369M cited 'changes in the macroeconomic outlook', and USCC build of $208M after a $232M release in Q2; Markets revenue -13% QoQ.
feedback.effect: supports the market's slowdown lean (credit and trading softening)
